title: A specified sheafification of a relation quotient has the coequalizer universal property
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site in a fixed choice of universes, and let $A,B$ be sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $s,t:B\rightrightarrows A$ be morphisms such that for every object $T$ the function $(s_T,t_T):B(T)\to A(T)^2$ is injective and its image $E_T$ is an equivalence relation. Let $P$ be the quotient presheaf $P(T)=A(T)/E_T$, with restrictions $[a]\mapsto[A(f)(a)]$ for $f:T'\to T$ and quotient map $\pi:A\to P$. Suppose a sheaf $Q$ and a morphism $\eta:P\to Q$ are a sheafification of this particular $P$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: composition with $\eta$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,H)$ for every sheaf $H$. Set $q=\eta\circ\pi$. Then $q\circ s=q\circ t$, and composition with $q$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{b:A\to H:b\circ s=b\circ t\}.$$
For an equalizing map $b$, the unique corresponding map $c:Q\to H$ satisfies $(c\circ\eta)_T([a])=b_T(a)$ for all $T,a$. Thus $(Q,q)$ is a coequalizer [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If $Z$ is any sheaf with $p:A\to Z$ that is also a coequalizer of $s,t$, the unique comparison $\alpha:Q\to Z$ with $\alpha\circ q=p$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the unique $\beta:Z\to Q$ with $\beta\circ p=q$, and $\alpha\beta=1_Z$, $\beta\alpha=1_Q$. Only the displayed universal property for this $P$ is assumed; a sheafification functor for all presheaves in these universes is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), universal property applied to the pointwise equivalence-relation quotient; compare Groupoids definition-quotient-sheaf and its following coequalizer paragraph in groupoids.tex. The comparison with any other coequalizer is uniqueness of the universal factorization.

proof.text: The statement already defines P as the chosen presheaf coequalizer of s.hom and t.hom. Mathlib coequalizer.condition_assoc therefore proves that q = π ≫ η equalizes s and t, after applying the faithful inclusion of sheaves into presheaves. The sectionwise quotient construction need not be rebuilt. The hypotheses on the image relation identify this chosen coequalizer with the quotient described in the statement; the universal-property argument works for any parallel pair.

source.place: Tag 02VG, coequalizer paragraph following definition-quotient-sheaf; Mathlib coequalizer.condition_assoc.

proof.text: Given b:A→H equalizing s,t, apply the presheaf coequalizer universal property to b.hom, obtaining d with π ≫ d = b.hom. Surjectivity of the specified hη gives c:Q→H with η ≫ c.hom = d, so q ≫ c = b. If q ≫ c′ = b, coequalizer.hom_ext gives η ≫ c′.hom = η ≫ c.hom, and injectivity of hη yields c′ = c. This proves the unique factorization hfactor without assuming a global sheafification functor.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint, specified factorization property; Categories Tag 002F.

proof.text: For any cofork k, apply hfactor to its arrow k.π and equation k.condition. Cofork.IsColimit.ofExistsUnique assembles these unique factorizations into IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ q hq). Cofork.IsColimit.homIso then gives the asserted equivalence with equalizing arrows, with forward map definitionally composition by q.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit, specialized to a parallel pair.

proof.text: For the unique c supplied by hfactor, apply the inclusion on homs to q ≫ c = b, then evaluate this equality at T and a. Since q.hom = π ≫ η, the resulting equation is exactly (η ≫ c.hom)_T(π_T(a)) = b_T(a). Uniqueness of c for the conjunction follows already from its first conjunct.

source.place: Tag 02VG, quotient-presheaf representative formula and coequalizer paragraph.

proof.text: For another colimiting cofork (Z,p), hfactor yields the unique α with q ≫ α = p, and its colimit property yields the unique β with p ≫ β = q. Precompose β ≫ α and 1_Z by p; associativity and the two factorization equations make them equal, so the other cofork hom_ext gives β ≫ α = 1_Z. Similarly precompose α ≫ β and 1_Q by q and use the constructed cofork hom_ext. These equations give IsIso α with inverse β. The same unique factorizations prove the nested uniqueness claims.

source.place: Tag 002F, uniqueness of colimits by unique factorization.

lean.statement: theorem specified_sheafified_relation_coequalizer {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A B : Sheaf J (Type w)) (s t : B ⟶ A) (hinj : ∀ T : C, Function.Injective (fun r : B.obj.obj (op T) ↦ (s.hom.app (op T) r, t.hom.app (op T) r))) (hrel : ∀ T : C, _root_.Equivalence (fun a b : A.obj.obj (op T) ↦ ∃ r : B.obj.obj (op T), s.hom.app (op T) r = a ∧ t.hom.app (op T) r = b)) (Q : Sheaf J (Type w)) (η : coequalizer s.hom t.hom ⟶ Q.obj) (hη : ∀ H : Sheaf J (Type w), Function.Bijective (fun c : Q ⟶ H ↦ η ≫ c.hom)) : ∃ hq : s ≫ specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η = t ≫ specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η, (∀ H : Sheaf J (Type w), ∃ e : (Q ⟶ H) ≃ {b : A ⟶ H // s ≫ b = t ≫ b}, ∀ c : Q ⟶ H, (e c).val = specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η ≫ c) ∧ (∀ (H : Sheaf J (Type w)) (b : A ⟶ H), s ≫ b = t ≫ b → ∃! c : Q ⟶ H, specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η ≫ c = b ∧ ∀ (T : C) (a : A.obj.obj (op T)), (η ≫ c.hom).app (op T) ((coequalizer.π s.hom t.hom).app (op T) a) = b.hom.app (op T) a) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ (specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η) hq)) ∧ (∀ (Z : Sheaf J (Type w)) (p : A ⟶ Z) (hp : s ≫ p = t ≫ p), IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ p hp) → ∃! α : Q ⟶ Z, specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η ≫ α = p ∧ IsIso α ∧ ∃! β : Z ⟶ Q, p ≫ β = specifiedRelationQuotientMap s t Q η ∧ β ≫ α = 𝟙 Z ∧ α ≫ β = 𝟙 Q)
